$comment: D-Fence pest profile catalogue. Traces: 4.2.1-4.2.3, 4.2.6, 4.2.7, 4.3.1-4.3.8, 8.6.2, 8.6.3, 1.5.2, 10.6.2. Severity multipliers and their rubric: PEST-PRIORITY-MODEL.md §4. Evidence tiers and the measurements behind them: §3. Driver weight sets: §5. Like config/scoring.default.json these are a team proposal, not fitted values.
$severityNote: sigma = rawSeverity/18 divided by the catalogue maximum (12/18), so Mosquito and Rat sit at exactly 1.000. That normalisation is what makes 4.2.5 hold: the mosquito score is unchanged from v0.8 and the tier thresholds at 40.0/70.0 still mean what SCORING-SPEC.md §4 says they mean. 4.2.7 refuses a catalogue in which no pest carries 1.0.
$contactNote: NEA 6225 5632 verified against nea.gov.sg/contact-us on 2026-09-16. AVS Animal Response Centre 1800 476 1600 verified against nparks.gov.sg/contact-us the same day.
$authorityNote: RESOLVED 2026-09-19 (was open point 10). BeeWasp goes to NPARKS and HouseCrow, Pigeon and JavanMyna go to AVS, because those are the channels the authorities themselves publish to residents. AVS lists house crows, pigeons and Javan mynas together under Encountering Wildlife and gives the Animal Response Centre, 1800 476 1600 (avs.nparks.gov.sg/wildlife/encountering-wildlife/house-crows-pigeons-javan-mynas/, read 2026-09-19). AVS's bees and wasps page gives a DIFFERENT number - the NParks Helpline, 1800 471 7300 (avs.nparks.gov.sg/wildlife/encountering-wildlife/bees-and-wasps/, read 2026-09-19) - which is why NPARKS is a separate authority here rather than a fourth pest pointed at AVS. The earlier provisional NEA setting had an argument behind it (D-Fence covers built-up municipal estates, which is the NEA side of the split) but it loses to the published channel: 8.6.3 shows a resident an authority and a number to call, and a resident who calls NEA about a bee hive has been sent to the wrong place by us. NEA remains the licensing authority for the pest control operators who do the removal - that is a different fact from who a resident reports to.
$taxonNote: iNaturalist taxon ids, each resolved by id against api.inaturalist.org/v1/taxa on 2026-09-16 rather than by name search. Name search is unsafe here: q=Serpentes returns 26172, which is Squamata - the whole order, including skinks and monitor lizards - and overcounts snakes roughly threefold. Serpentes is 85553.

A.$comment: 4.3.4. Byte-identical to config/scoring.default.json. 4.2.5 depends on it.

B.$comment: 4.3.5. Reports lead, because a report is a complaint and an observation is not (4.1.26). ResponseCapacityDeficit is deliberately small: the VCO registry holds registered offices, not service areas.

C.$comment: 4.3.6. Tier B with the external driver's 0.20 redistributed onto the two report drivers, which are the only evidence a tier C pest has (4.3.10).

pests.$raw: 4+2+3+3 = 12; tier C because 128 iNat records a year is too thin to move a driver
2+4+3+2 = 11; tier C because 30/30 sampled records were location-obscured
4+0+3+2 = 9; Diptera order-wide, a coarse density signal only
4+2+2+1 = 9; ONE iNat record in twelve months
0+6+2+1 = 9; NParks Helpline, not the Animal Response Centre - see $authorityNote
0+2+2+2 = 6; ONE iNat record in twelve months - indoor pests are invisible to a biodiversity platform
5.1.15 requires a value for a pest the resident cannot name. Scored at the catalogue floor and from reports alone: an unidentified pest is evidence of something, and the moderator decides what.

criticalOverrideRules.$comment: 4.4.1-4.4.3. A linear weighted sum cannot express acute life-safety: a snake indoors in a two-report locality scores low and is right to score low, and is still the thing the manager must see first. These raise the TIER and never the score (4.4.5).
